text: Write a short essay, around 400 words, arguing that cities should charge for street parking at market rates. Take a clear position and address the strongest objection.
Write a story of about 500 words in which a lighthouse keeper receives a letter that was posted forty years earlier. Keep it quiet and unsentimental; no twist ending.
Describe a crowded night market in the rain from the point of view of someone who has just lost their wallet. Three paragraphs, present tense, no dialogue.

Draft a polite but firm letter to a landlord explaining that the heating has been broken for eleven days, that two repair appointments were missed, and that I intend to withhold rent proportionally until it is fixed. Keep it under 300 words and avoid threats.
Write a personal essay opening, roughly 250 words, about learning to cook from a grandparent who never measured anything. It should end on a concrete image rather than a moral.

Write a scene, about 600 words, in which two old colleagues meet by chance at an airport gate after a falling-out years ago. Mostly dialogue. Neither of them apologises, but by the end something has shifted.
Write a product description for a hand-thrown ceramic pour-over coffee dripper. Warm but not gushing, 120 to 160 words, mention the glaze, the weight, and that no two are identical.

Compose a wedding toast from the perspective of the groom's older sister. Two minutes spoken, so around 280 words. One funny childhood anecdote, one sincere line, no inside jokes the room would not get.
Write a descriptive paragraph of a disused railway cutting in late autumn, focusing on sound and smell more than sight. Around 150 words.
Write a 700-word short story told entirely through a series of voicemail transcripts left by a daughter for her father over the course of one winter.

Write an opinion piece of about 450 words for a company newsletter making the case that meetings should default to 25 minutes instead of 30. Include one concrete suggestion for how to run the shorter version.

Write a cover letter for a junior data analyst role at a regional public transport authority. I have a geography degree, a year of volunteer work cleaning survey data for a housing charity, and I am comfortable with SQL and spreadsheets but have never used Python professionally. Around 300 words, and do not oversell.
Describe the interior of a small-town hardware store that has been run by the same family for three generations. Focus on the details that reveal who works there. About 200 words.
Write a fable, no more than 350 words, in which a heron and a river argue about who truly owns the fish. Give it a moral, but let the moral be slightly uncomfortable.
Write a reflective essay of roughly 500 words on the experience of moving back to a childhood town as an adult and finding it both smaller and larger than remembered.
Write a thank-you note to a neighbour who looked after my dog for two weeks while I was in hospital. Warm, specific, under 150 words, and mention the dog by name: Biscuit.
Write the opening 400 words of a mystery novel set on a container ship. Establish the narrator, the setting and one small wrong detail that the reader should notice before the narrator does.
Write a eulogy of about 350 words for a retired maths teacher, delivered by a former student who did badly in her class and only later understood what she had been trying to teach.

Write a travel-magazine style piece, around 450 words, about a fictional island whose only town shuts down entirely on Wednesdays. Explain the custom through the people you meet rather than through exposition.
Write a letter from a parent to a child who is leaving for university, to be opened on the first night away. Honest, a little awkward, no more than 250 words, and it should not try to give advice.
Write a monologue, about 300 words, for a stage play: a night-shift baker talking to an apprentice on their first shift about why the bread is always slightly different on windy nights.
Write 200 words describing the feeling of stepping outside after a long illness, concentrating on how ordinary things seem newly strange.
Write a persuasive essay of around 550 words arguing that public libraries should lend tools and musical instruments as well as books. Anticipate the funding objection and the liability objection.
Write a very short story, under 200 words, in which the entire plot turns on a mislabelled jar in a shared office fridge.
